Being around people in authority or uniform
Seeing people that I socialised with before the event

Threat.value: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places
Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard

Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank
I cannot tell a clear story of what happened even to myself

vignette: John, a 56-year-old European-American musician married to his long-time partner, has been struggling with the aftermath of a sexual assault that occurred two years ago. The event still haunts him deeply, and he finds himself frequently reliving fragments of it through vivid yet incomplete memories. John recalls being assaulted while out at a local concert, where the perpetrator wore a distinct cologne that lingers in his mind like a haunting melody. Since then, any encounter with this specific fragrance immediately triggers intense fear and panic, bringing him back to the night of the assault. He has become acutely sensitive to sudden movements and violent imagery, which also serve as powerful reminders of that traumatic event. John’s memory of the incident is fragmented and disjointed. Some moments are crystal clear, while others remain shrouded in darkness, making it nearly impossible for him to piece together a coherent narrative. This fragmented memory has led him to suppress any feelings or thoughts related to the assault, as confronting these emotions feels too overwhelming. His tendency to push away painful memories only exacerbates his sense of threat and anxiety. The assault shattered John’s sense of security. He now feels safe in only a very limited number of places and is constantly on guard. The sudden movements of others can trigger immediate reactions of irritability and aggression, as he remains hypervigilant to potential threats. This heightened state of alertness makes it particularly difficult for him to interact with authority figures or people in uniform, whom he perceives as potentially dangerous. John has become increasingly isolated, avoiding social contacts and even colleagues from his past life as a musician. He feels that seeing these familiar faces might trigger painful memories and lead to further emotional distress. This avoidance strategy, however, only reinforces the sense of threat and anxiety, creating a cycle where fear becomes self-perpetuating. The more he avoids situations and people, the more they loom in his mind as potential threats. One particular incident at a recent concert brought this cycle into sharp focus. John was playing with a group of old friends when someone sprayed a cologne similar to that worn by the perpetrator. Instantly, he felt a wave of nausea and fear, triggering an angry outburst towards those around him. This reaction strained his relationships with these musicians, who had always been close friends, leaving him feeling more isolated and alone. John’s memory issues have also played a significant role in his current state. The fragments of the assault that do come to mind are so vivid and disturbing that he finds it nearly impossible to function without suppressing them entirely. This suppression, however, only serves to intensify his fear and anxiety, making even minor triggers feel overwhelming. The trauma has deeply affected John’s life as a musician. He used to perform regularly at venues across the city but now avoids almost all public performances out of fear that something might trigger another panic attack or violent memory. His wife reports that he is often irritable and withdrawn, and his relationships have suffered as a result. John’s current state reflects a complex interplay between triggers, threat perceptions, maladaptive strategies, and fragmented memories. The more he suppresses his emotions and avoids situations, the more intense his reactions to potential triggers become. This self-reinforcing cycle has left him feeling trapped and unable to move forward. Ultimately, it was the escalating impact on his personal relationships that finally prompted John to seek help. He is most afraid of losing those closest to him due to his volatile behavior but also hopes for a way to reclaim control over his life and find peace with his past.
